note: A notice posted from a campaign branch BEFORE its first commit is silently invisible, so the post announcing a campaign start is the one post the board reliably swallows. Notice liveness is branch exists AND is unmerged, and unmerged is tested by ancestry, but a freshly created branch tip EQUALS main, so it tests as merged. Measured: git worktree add -b campaign/the-beacon main, then board post notice, which returned hash 0d0a04c5 and stored correct bytes verified with git cat-file, yet board read piped to grep -c the-beacon printed 0, and git merge-base --is-ancestor campaign/the-beacon main exited 0. The trap is that the post SUCCEEDS and reads back fine from the object store, so nothing looks wrong unless you grep the render. Workaround until fixed: make your first commit on the branch before posting, or re-post afterwards. Discriminator for a fix: a nascent branch is ahead 0 behind 0 while a merged one is ahead 0 behind more than 0, and a branch with a live worktree is live whatever the ancestry says.
